name: Convex polygon separating-axis intersection test
definition: For two full-dimensional closed convex planar polygons P,Q, take every nonzero edge normal a from both polygons. Set I_P(a)=[min_{p in P} a·p,max_{p in P} a·p] and likewise I_Q(a). Declare disjoint iff at least one axis has max I_P < min I_Q or max I_Q < min I_P; otherwise report intersection including boundary contact.
variables: P,Q ordered convex polygon vertices; a nonzero perpendicular to an edge; I_P,I_Q scalar projection intervals.
assumptions: Finite cyclic convex polygon vertices with positive area, no zero-length edges, exact comparisons or an explicitly justified robust predicate.
limitations: Direct projection costs O((m+n)^2) arithmetic for m,n vertices; not valid for arbitrary nonconvex polygons; no contact manifold or penetration depth returned.
failure_conditions: Invalid convexity or zero area, nonfinite coordinates, zero-length edge, or unreliable comparison near touching.
computation: Enumerate perpendicular edge vectors from both boundaries; compute min/max dot products without normalizing; early exit on strict interval separation; equality means touching or overlap.

source.citation: Provisional source locator: Michael Lugo, Fun with the Separating Axis Theorem, Virginia Tech, https://personal.math.vt.edu/mrlugo/sat.html ; independent review pending.

name: Minimum enclosing disk by support enumeration
definition: For nonempty finite P in R², minimize r² over disks (c,r) with ||p−c||² ≤ r² for all p in P. Enumerate centers at individual points, midpoints of distinct pairs, and circumcenters of noncollinear triples; associate squared radius of the defining support; discard disks not containing all P and choose minimum squared radius.
variables: P finite planar points, c disk center, r nonnegative radius, support of size one to three.
assumptions: Finite nonempty planar input, Euclidean metric, exact arithmetic or robust containment and collinearity tests; duplicate points allowed.
limitations: O(n^4) arithmetic for exhaustive candidate generation and containment; not the randomized Welzl algorithm; near-collinearity may amplify floating-point error.
failure_conditions: Empty or nonfinite input, inaccurate circumcenter or containment predicates.
computation: Test singleton disks, pair diameter disks and noncollinear triple circumdisks; skip collinear triples, retain only containing disks; minimize squared radius.

source.citation: Provisional source locator: CGAL Min_circle_2 reference at Stanford, https://www.graphics.stanford.edu/courses/cs368-00-spring/TA/manuals/CGAL/ref-manual2/Optimisation/Min_circle_2.html ; independent review pending.
